speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and the sudden onset of periumbilical pain with bloody stools, I am concerned about intestinal ischemia. I will immediately order a CT angiogram of the abdomen and pelvis to check for blood flow issues in your mesenteric arteries. REQUEST TEST: CT_Angiogram_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT angiogram confirms mesenteric ischemia, likely secondary to your recent myocardial infarction. I am proceeding with urgent surgical consultation for potential bowel resection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia
